subject: Business Models
title: Negative Pricing
description: A micro-lesson that makes Negative Pricing usable.

hook.text: Google pays Apple $20 billion per year to be the default search engine on iPhones. Google pays you to use it.

buildup.text: Negative pricing means the company pays the customer (or their gatekeeper) to use the product.

discovery.text: When the user's attention is the product, companies compete by paying distributors and customers for access.

twist.text: Credit card companies pay users via cashback. The merchants pay the fees. Users get paid to spend money.

climax.text: Negative pricing flips economics upside down. When data and attention are valuable, access is worth paying for.

punchline.text: $20B to be the default. When attention is the product, the user gets paid.

quiz.question: Why does Google pay Apple $20 billion per year?
options: To be the default search engine on iPhones
